subject.title: feat(drive): add one-way recursive directory push

question: Should gog own a first-class one-way recursive Drive push workflow with the proposed fail-before-mutation reconciliation semantics?
rationale: The capability is aligned with supported Drive automation, but it creates a new multi-object mutation contract whose ambiguity, failure, and proof rules cannot be selected safely from existing primitives alone.

options.title: Sponsor narrow push
options.body: Approve the bounded no-delete workflow and require a written preflight and partial-failure contract plus live My Drive and shared-drive proof before landing.

options.title: Keep primitives only
options.body: Decline a first-class sync command and continue requiring callers to compose upload, replace, mkdir, listing, and checksum logic externally.

options.title: Revise the contract
options.body: Keep the issue open for a smaller command shape or different ambiguity and recovery semantics before implementation begins.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrow push
recommendation.body: Approve the bounded no-delete workflow and require a written preflight and partial-failure contract plus live My Drive and shared-drive proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent release and prior partial-landing history make steipete the best available owner for the command-surface decision.
